cues.en: We mentioned activation functions in passing earlier but let's go into a little bit more depth as they are an important concept.
cues.zh: 前面簡單提過激活函數，但它是重要概念，再深入一點。

cues.en: It turns out there's many different kinds of activation functions you can choose from and picking the right one can be important, for the performance of your neural network.
cues.zh: 有很多不同激活函數可以選，選對函數，可能對神經網路效能很重要。

cues.en: Now an activation function is just the function inside of a given node or neuron whatever you want to call it.
cues.zh: 激活函數，就是某個節點或神經元裡的函數。

cues.en: That sums up all of the incoming inputs into that neuron and decides what output it should then send out to the next layer of neuron.
cues.zh: 將進入該神經元的所有輸入加總，再決定要向下一層神經元送出什麼輸出。

cues.en: So it's just that function that says "given the inputs what should my output be".
cues.zh: 也就是回答：「給定這些輸入，輸出應該是什麼？」

cues.en: That's all an activation function is. Now the simplest activation function is called the linear activation function.
cues.zh: 激活函數就是這樣。最簡單的，叫做線性激活函數。

cues.en: And all this does is output whatever it got as an input it's just a straight line there.
cues.zh: 它只是把收到的輸入直接輸出，就是一條直線。

cues.en: The problem with a linear activation function is that it doesn't really do anything.
cues.zh: 問題是，線性激活函數，其實沒做什麼。

cues.en: It's just a mirroring what came into it as an output.
cues.zh: 只是把輸入原樣映射成輸出。

cues.en: So as a result it can't really do any interesting learning, it can't do any backpropagation as it's actually going back and learning through the network and trying to optimize things.
cues.zh: 因此，無法做有趣的學習，也無法在網路中向後學習、最佳化時，進行反向傳播。

cues.en: And also because it's just outputting whatever it got as an input, there's really no point to having multiple layers at all with a linear activation function.
cues.zh: 而且因為只是把輸入原樣輸出，使用線性激活函數時，多層根本沒有意義。

cues.en: If it's just turning around and putting the input of one layer as the output to the next layer, there's really no point in having more than one layer because it's just going to be the same thing all the way through.
cues.zh: 如果只是把這層輸入，當成下一層輸出，那超過一層就沒意義，因為從頭到尾都相同。

cues.en: So linear activation functions actually aren't very useful you don't really see these in action very much at all. Sort of the close cousin to a linear activation function would be the binary step function.
cues.zh: 因此，線性激活函數其實不太實用，也不常看到。它的近親，是二元階躍函數。

cues.en: And all this does is say well if I have nothing coming in to the neuron then I'm going to output nothing.
cues.zh: 它只是說，如果神經元沒有任何輸入，就沒有輸出。

cues.en: But if anything at all is coming in I'm gonna output a positive value.
cues.zh: 但只要有任何輸入，就輸出正值。

cues.en: That's a fixed value so it's either on or off.
cues.zh: 那是固定值，因此不是開就是關。

cues.en: The problem with this well there's a few problems.
cues.zh: 問題是，嗯，有幾個問題。

cues.en: First of all it can't handle any multiple classification.
cues.zh: 首先，不能處理多重分類。

cues.en: It's a binary function it can only be on or off.
cues.zh: 它是二元函數，只能開或關。

cues.en: It can only signal that this neuron represents one thing.
cues.zh: 只能表示這個神經元代表一件事。

cues.en: Right.
cues.zh: 對吧？

cues.en: So if you want to say that a given thing belongs to multiple categories there's no way to do that with a binary step function.
cues.zh: 如果想表示某個東西屬於多個類別，二元階躍函數做不到。

cues.en: I can only say that this belongs to a single category.
cues.zh: 只能說，它屬於單一類別。

cues.en: But the bigger problem is it's something that has to do with mathematics and calculus.
cues.zh: 但更大的問題，與數學和微積分有關。

cues.en: So as we're learning through this network, we have to do a bunch of derivatives on these activation functions as we do so and it turns out that vertical slopes and calculus really don't get along together.
cues.zh: 網路學習時，需要對激活函數做很多微分，但垂直斜率與微積分，其實不太合得來。

cues.en: The derivative of that would be infinite.
cues.zh: 它的導數會是無限大。

cues.en: And that just causes your math to blow up.
cues.zh: 這會讓數學運算出問題。

cues.en: That's why in this particular instance here, you're seeing that the step function isn't quite a step it's off to the side a little there it has a little bit of a slant to it. That's just to make the math not explode.
cues.zh: 因此，這個例子中的階躍函數，不是完全的階躍，而是稍微偏斜，帶一點斜率，只是為了避免數學運算崩潰。

cues.en: And when you find yourself doing things like that, to just make things not explode, that might be nature's way of telling you that what you're building is not very stable right.
cues.zh: 當你必須做這類事，才能避免運算崩潰，也許就是在提醒你，建立的東西不太穩定，對吧？

cues.en: So again binary step function is very simple in concept it's kind of like where they started with a neural networks back when they were first being developed. But they quickly found that they are very
cues.zh: 因此，二元階躍函數概念非常簡單，神經網路最初發展時，確實從這裡開始。但很快就發現，它們非常

cues.en: limited in how these mathematical problems.
cues.zh: 受限，而且有這些數學問題。

cues.en: So you don't really see them in use much today.
cues.zh: 因此，今天不太會使用。

cues.en: Instead we want to focus on nonlinear activation functions and the benefit of a nonlinear function is that you can create these complex mappings between inputs and outputs.
cues.zh: 我們改為專注非線性激活函數，好處是能建立複雜的輸入與輸出映射。

cues.en: So this more information there to be passed along from layer to layer and because they have a useful derivative, they're not just you know straight lines that are horizontal and vertical.
cues.zh: 因此，層與層之間能傳遞更多資訊，而且具有可用的導數，不只是水平或垂直直線。

cues.en: It allows you to do more interesting learning as you backpropagate and learned how to optimize these weights between the layers of your network.
cues.zh: 這讓反向傳播能做更有意思的學習，學會如何最佳化各層之間的權重。

cues.en: Also, they allow for multiple layers, because they aren't just a degenerate linear function that outputs whatever the input was, because they're more complicated you can actually have a benefit from having
cues.zh: 而且，不再是把輸入原樣輸出的退化線性函數，由於更複雜，神經網路就真的能從

cues.en: multiple layers to your neural network.
cues.zh: 多層結構獲益。

cues.en: So nonlinear is the way to go. So you might start with a function like this.
cues.zh: 所以，應該使用非線性。可以從這種函數開始。

cues.en: And on the top here we have what's called a sigmoid activation function which is also known as a logistic activation function that the same thing.
cues.zh: 上面是 Sigmoid 激活函數，也叫邏輯斯激活函數，是同一件事。

cues.en: And at the bottom we have what's called a 10 h or a hyperbolic tangent activation function again two different names for the same thing.
cues.zh: 下面是 tanh，也就是雙曲正切激活函數，同樣是同一件事的兩個名稱。

cues.en: The benefits of these are like we talked about they're nice and smooth they have nice pretty derivatives.
cues.zh: 優點如前所述，平滑連續，導數也很好。

cues.en: And the only real difference is that the sigmoid function on the top the logistic activation function will scale the outputs between 0 and 1, whereas the hyperbolic tangent function will scale everything
cues.zh: 唯一真正差異，是上面的 Sigmoid，也就是邏輯斯激活函數，將輸出縮放到零到一；雙曲正切則把所有值縮放到

cues.en: between negative 1 and positive 1.
cues.zh: 負一到正一。

cues.en: And generally speaking, when you're dealing with machine learning it's nice to have things with the mean around zero.
cues.zh: 一般來說，機器學習中，平均值在零附近會比較好。

cues.en: So in practice you'll find that the hyperbolic tangent function is the function of choice between these two.
cues.zh: 因此，實務上，兩者之間通常會選雙曲正切。

cues.en: You don't really see sigmoid or logistic functions being used. More often it's the hyperbolic tangent one that you're going to see in this sort of environment. And they're very well suited to recurrent
cues.zh: 不太會看到 Sigmoid 或邏輯斯函數，比較常看到雙曲正切。它們也很適合循環式

cues.en: neural networks as well.
cues.zh: 神經網路。

cues.en: They have some problems though. So one problem is that as you get toward the extreme positive or negative values here of the inputs. The output starts to change very slowly right.
cues.zh: 不過有一些問題。輸入接近很大的正值或負值時，輸出開始變得非常緩慢，對吧？

cues.en: So if you imagine these graphs stretching out even further to the left or the right the change in those values becomes very very small.
cues.zh: 想像圖繼續向左或向右延伸，數值變化會非常非常小。

cues.en: And this is what we call the vanishing gradient problem.
cues.zh: 這就叫做梯度消失問題。

cues.en: It's actually get to the point where numerical precision issues can become a problem at a given point and we'll talk about the vanishing gradient problem in more detail later in the course.
cues.zh: 最後甚至可能出現數值精度問題，課程稍後會更深入介紹梯度消失。

cues.en: But this is where it comes from.
cues.zh: 這就是它的來源。

cues.en: That's one of the downsides of using a sigmoid logistic 10 H or hyperbolic tangent activation function.
cues.zh: 這是使用 Sigmoid、邏輯斯、tanh 或雙曲正切激活函數的缺點之一。

cues.en: They're also computationally expensive. Computers aren't very good at doing trigonometry very quickly so if you do use a complex activation function like this it tends to take a longer time for your neural
cues.zh: 運算成本也高。電腦不太擅長快速做三角函數，因此使用這種複雜激活函數，通常會讓神經網路

cues.en: networks to converge and to actually do their learning. So an answer to that is what's called the rectified linear unit or ReLu for short.
cues.zh: 花更多時間收斂、學習。一個解法，是修正線性單元，簡稱 ReLU。

cues.en: This is a very popular choice these days. Very simple as you can see it's just a linear straight line on the positive side and just a flat zero on the negative side.
cues.zh: 這是現在很熱門的選擇。如你所見，非常簡單，正值側是一條直線，負值側是平坦的零。

cues.en: So kind of has a lot in common with a binary step function except it's not a step.
cues.zh: 因此，與二元階躍函數有很多共通處，只是它不是階躍。

cues.en: It's actually more of a slant off to the right there right.
cues.zh: 而是向右上方傾斜，對吧？

cues.en: The main benefit of this is that it's very easy and fast to compute.
cues.zh: 主要優點，是非常容易、快速計算。

cues.en: So computers are very efficient at computing straight lines right.
cues.zh: 電腦很擅長算直線，對吧？

cues.en: So as opposed to trigonometry.
cues.zh: 相較於三角函數。

cues.en: So it's very quick to have a model converge using a simple function like this.
cues.zh: 因此，用這麼簡單的函數，模型能很快收斂。

cues.en: So that's a good thing.
cues.zh: 這是好事。

cues.en: And it's no vertical lines in this either.
cues.zh: 而且，這裡也沒有垂直線。

cues.en: So you don't have to have any you know weird calculus problems resulting from vertical gradients and the infinities that result from that.
cues.zh: 因此，不必擔心垂直梯度與無限大，造成奇怪的微積分問題。

cues.en: There are some downsides over to ReLu even though it is a popular choice and a very fast and efficient choice and that's that when we have zero or negative values we do generate back to a linear function
cues.zh: 雖然 ReLU 很熱門、快速、有效率，仍有缺點：數值為零或負值時，這裡又退化成線性函數，

cues.en: here and all the problems that come along with that.
cues.zh: 並帶來相關問題。

cues.en: This is known as the dying ReLu problem and in a lot of cases, it's not really an issue. But there are some models where that can actually cause trouble.
cues.zh: 這叫做 ReLU 死亡問題。很多情況沒事，但有些模型確實會有麻煩。

cues.en: So the solution to the dying ReLu problem is simply to not have it go flat on the negative side but have it sloped down it's sort of a shallow angle there instead.
cues.zh: 解法是，不讓負值側平坦，而是以平緩角度，向下傾斜。

cues.en: This just introduces a small negative slope, when you go below zero on the x-axis, and usually, it's not as steep as that usually is going to be a little bit closer to horizontal there but that's the idea
cues.zh: 也就是 X 軸低於零時，引入一個小的負向斜坡，通常不會像圖中那麼陡，而是更接近水平，這就是

cues.en: of Leakey ReLu instead of a straight flat horizontal line to the left.
cues.zh: Leaky ReLU 的概念，不再讓左側是完全平坦的水平線。

cues.en: We slow, slow it down a little bit instead.
cues.zh: 而是讓它稍微傾斜。

cues.en: But how do you know what slope is best.
cues.zh: 但怎麼知道什麼斜率最好？

cues.en: Right.
cues.zh: 對吧？

cues.en: Like you can just decide arbitrarily and some people do that.
cues.zh: 可以任意決定，有些人確實這麼做。

cues.en: But a better way would be something called parametric ReLu or PreLu for short.
cues.zh: 但更好的方式，是參數式 ReLU，簡稱 PReLU。

cues.en: And this is exactly the same thing as Leakey ReLu.
cues.zh: 與 Leaky ReLU 完全相同，

cues.en: But the slope in the negative part is learned via backpropagation itself.
cues.zh: 只是負值部分的斜率，也由反向傳播自行學習。

cues.en: So as we're going back and learning all the weights between the nodes in our neural network. We're also learning the optimal slope for that negative portion of the ReLu activation function.
cues.zh: 因此，在反向學習神經網路節點間的所有權重時，也學習 ReLU 激活函數負值部分的最佳斜率。

cues.en: The downside of course is that this is very complicated and computationally intensive.
cues.zh: 缺點當然是，非常複雜、運算密集。

cues.en: So we're kind of throwing away some of the benefits of ReLu and your mileage may vary.
cues.zh: 因此，等於放棄一些 ReLU 的優點，成效可能因情況而異。

cues.en: Different kinds of problems will benefit from this more or less than others.
cues.zh: 不同問題，得到的好處可能多也可能少。

cues.en: So you'll find that in the majority of cases straight up ReLu or a constant Leakey ReLu will fit the bill.
cues.zh: 所以，多數情況，一般 ReLU 或固定斜率的 Leaky ReLU，就足夠。

cues.en: But if you do need to do better than that parametric ReLu or preLu is worth exploring and there are other variants of ReLu as well out there and is called the exponential linear unit that's shown
cues.zh: 但如果需要更好，值得探索參數式 ReLU，也就是 PReLU。還有其他 ReLU 變形，例如上方的指數線性單元，

cues.en: on the top here or ELU for short.
cues.zh: 簡稱 ELU。

cues.en: This is you know like leaky RELu but instead of a straight line on the negative side it's actually doing an exponential function instead.
cues.zh: 它像 Leaky ReLU，但負值側不是直線，而是指數函數。

cues.en: So again calculus tends to favor these sort of smoother curves here. So that can sometimes work out better than leaky ReLu.
cues.zh: 同樣地，微積分通常較適合這種平滑曲線，因此有時比 Leaky ReLU 更好。

cues.en: Also on the bottom here we have something that's pretty close to swish.
cues.zh: 下方也有一個很接近 Swish 的函數。

cues.en: This is a function that was developed by Google and it performs really well.
cues.zh: 這是 Google 開發的函數，效果很好。

cues.en: It's a good alternative to ReLu or leaky ReLu or any of this stuff.
cues.zh: 是 ReLU、Leaky ReLU 等函數的好替代方案。

cues.en: Mostly you see a benefit with swish.
cues.zh: Swish 的好處，主要在

cues.en: If you have really really deep networks. You need to have like 40 or more layers to really start seeing a benefit from swish.
cues.zh: 非常深的網路中。大約 40 層以上，才開始真正看到效益。

cues.en: One other variant is called max out and that's a very simple function that just outputs the maximum of all of the inputs that came into that node. And technically ReLu'sa special case of that mathematically
cues.zh: 另一種變形叫做 Maxout，非常簡單，只輸出進入節點所有輸入中的最大值。嚴格從數學來說，ReLU 是它的特殊

cues.en: speaking.
cues.zh: 情況。

cues.en: However max out doubles the number of parameters that you need to train it.
cues.zh: 不過，Maxout 會讓需要訓練的參數數量加倍。

cues.en: So it's not really practical in practice.
cues.zh: 因此，實務上不太實用。

cues.en: It's gonna be very expensive to do and you know it's usually not worth the effort of actually doing
cues.zh: 成本非常高，通常不值得真正費力去做。

cues.en: that. One more activation function we need to talk about is soft Max and you often see this as the final output layer of a multiple classification problem.
cues.zh: 就是這樣。還有一個要談的激活函數，是 softmax，常用在多類別分類問題的最後輸出層。

cues.en: So if you have a one-hot encoded classification like you know what object is in this picture.
cues.zh: 例如，使用獨熱編碼分類，判斷圖片中是什麼物體，

cues.en: Things like that. Often you will see softmax apply to see activation function on the final output layer of that neural network.
cues.zh: 這類問題，通常會看到神經網路最後輸出層，使用 softmax 作為激活函數。

cues.en: And what softmax does is it takes those outputs from that last layer and converts them into probabilities for each classification.
cues.zh: Softmax 把最後一層輸出，轉成每個類別的機率。

cues.en: So it allows us to take the output of this neural network that's trying to classify something and interpret those final outputs of the probabilities of that thing being in each one of those classifications.
cues.zh: 讓我們能把這個分類神經網路的最終輸出，解讀成某個東西屬於各類別的機率。

cues.en: And if you need to choose you know, which classification is the best guess, you can just take the maximum one out of that set of outputs.
cues.zh: 如果需要選出最佳分類猜測，只要從這組輸出取最大值。

cues.en: Another thing is that well can't produce more than one label for something still.
cues.zh: 另外，它仍無法為同一個東西產生多個標籤。

cues.en: So if you do have a case where you want to say that this picture contains this thing and this thing is this thing, it can't really do that's gonna pick one of the other sigmoid activation functions.
cues.zh: 因此，如果想說這張圖同時包含這個、那個與另一個東西，它無法真正做到，只會選其中一個。而 Sigmoid 激活函數，

cues.en: However are good for more than one label for something you know multiple classification.
cues.zh: 則適合為同一個東西指定多個標籤，也就是多重分類。

cues.en: OK so that's an important distinction.
cues.zh: 這是重要區別。

cues.en: That's another thing that's sigmoid is good for. Now you don't have to worry about the actual guts of the softmax function itself or the exam. You just need to know what it's used for, it's for multiple classification
cues.zh: 這也是 Sigmoid 擅長的事。考試不必擔心 softmax 內部細節，只要知道用途：多類別分類，

cues.en: and converting the outputs of a neural network into probabilities of each given classification that each neuron represents. So that's a lot of activation functions.
cues.zh: 將神經網路輸出，轉成每個神經元代表類別的機率。介紹了好多激活函數。

cues.en: How do you choose one?
cues.zh: 該如何選？

cues.en: Well it's not that hard really.
cues.zh: 其實不難。

cues.en: So if you're gonna be doing multiple classification Were you just trying to pick one classification for an object, you want to use softmax on the output layer, that's what soft Max is for if you have a
cues.zh: 如果做多類別分類，只想替物件選一個類別，就在輸出層用 softmax，這正是它的用途。如果是

cues.en: recurrent neural network those tend to do well with 10 H or hyperbolic tangent activation functions two names for the same thing. For everything else you might wanna start with ReLu and if Relu not
cues.zh: 循環神經網路，tanh，也就是雙曲正切，通常很好，兩者是同一件事的不同名稱。其餘情況，可以先從 ReLU 開始，如果

cues.en: good enough, try leaky Relu If leaky Relu is not good enough try preLu or maybe even max out. If you have a really really deep neural network with 40 or more layers you might wanna look at something
cues.zh: 不夠好，試 Leaky ReLU；還不夠，試 PReLU，甚至 Maxout。如果是 40 層以上的非常深神經網路，可能想研究

cues.en: like swish instead.
